children: Credit card delinquencies and charge-offs ticked up in August compared to the prior month, according to Seeking Alpha's latest edition of Credit Pulse.
Charge-off rate is the percentage of loans that banks write off as uncollectible.
Seeking Alpha tracks delinquency and charge-off numbers for seven banks in its monthly roundup: American Express (
Average delinquencies across the seven banks rose to 2.51% in August from 2.50%, above the three-month average of 2.50%. However, the figure remained below the year-ago level of 2.67%.
August delinquencies were above the pre-pandemic average of 2.48%.
Meanwhile, net charge-offs across the banks increased to 3.29% from 3.28%, but were below the three-month average of 3.33%.
A year ago, charge-offs averaged 3.74%, while the figure came to 3.57% for August 2019.
Notably, revolving consumer credit outstanding rose at an annual rate of 2.48% in July 2026, slowing from the June 2026 pace of 5.98% and the July 2025 pace of 7.87%.

Meanwhile, a recent Bank of America research note said total U.S. credit and debit card spending per household rose 4.5% year-over-year in August. Spending excluding gas was up 3.7%, implying heavy reliance on credit to cover everyday expenses amid higher inflation.
